recognize_zh: 背景幾乎每個紅血球都有細小的環狀體（ring form），不少紅血球含兩個以上環或雙染色質點，並見貼附在紅血球邊緣的 appliqué 型，呈高度寄生率的惡性瘧（P. falciparum）；下方中性球細胞質內可見褐黑色瘧色素（hemozoin）顆粒。
features: Very high parasitemia with delicate small ring forms in a large proportion of red cells
Multiply infected red cells, double chromatin dots and marginal appliqué (accolé) forms
Infected red cells are not enlarged and lack Schüffner stippling
One segmented neutrophil containing coarse brown-black hemozoin granules in its cytoplasm; a second neutrophil without pigment
No mature schizonts seen; scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a very high parasitemia with numerous small delicate ring forms, frequent multiply infected red cells, double chromatin dots and appliqué forms, in normal-sized red cells without stippling. A segmented neutrophil contains coarse brown-black intracytoplasmic pigment consistent with phagocytosed hemozoin, while an adjacent neutrophil lacks pigment. Schizonts are not identified. Findings are consistent with heavy Plasmodium falciparum infection with pigment-laden neutrophils, a marker of severe malaria.

ddx.vs: Babesia also produces multiple small rings but shows tetrad (Maltese cross) forms and never produces hemozoin pigment.
These infect enlarged red cells with Schüffner stippling and show amoeboid trophozoites and schizonts, with multiple infection being uncommon.
Toxic granules are dark purple-blue, fine and evenly distributed, whereas hemozoin is refractile brown-black and coarse.
Superimposed platelets sit above the red cell plane, lack a ring cytoplasm with a chromatin dot and show a halo.
